What are the rules for merge rules: which sub-divisions can be merged?

Survey Number Merging:
- Combines multiple survey numbers or sub-divisions into single survey number
- Used when adjacent land parcels are purchased by same owner
- Simplifies land records and patta management

Merge Eligibility Criteria:

1. Common Ownership
   - All survey numbers must have same owner
   - Ownership must be sole (not joint) or all joint owners must agree
   - Patta holder name must match across all surveys

2. Geographic Adjacency
   - Survey numbers must share common boundary
   - Non-adjacent surveys cannot be merged
   - At least one common boundary point required

3. Same Jurisdiction
   - All surveys must belong to same block
   - Surveys from different blocks cannot be merged
   - Surveys must be in same ward and town

4. Same Land Classification
   - All surveys must have same land type (agricultural, residential, commercial)

Explain what is a field visit

Definition: A field visit (also called a field inspection or site inspection) is
the on-site verification an SIS officer carries out at the actual land parcel
before an application can move forward. The officer goes to the survey number in
person, instead of deciding the application from the documents alone.

What the officer does during a field visit:
- Locates the survey number and its sub-division on the ground
- Measures the actual boundaries and area, and compares them with the patta
  and the sale deed
- Marks the survey corners and checks the boundary stones
- Checks for encroachment or any occupation that does not match the record
- Obtains the signatures of the applicant and of all joint owners
- Takes photographs and prepares preliminary field notes and a rough sketch

When an ISD application is processed, the Deputy Inspector Surveyor (DIS)
assigns temporary subdivision numbers to each proposed parcel before the
final numbers are confirmed.

Format: {existing_subdivision}/T{sequence}
- The part before /T is the existing subdivision being split
  (0 when the parent survey has no prior subdivision)
- T stands for "Temporary"
- The number after T is a sequence counter (1, 2, 3...) for each new parcel

  row.
- Encumbrance Certificate must show a clear title for the preceding 13 years and
  be within 3 months of its issue date at the time of verification.
- igrs_auto_mutation_flag = Y means mutation is expected to post automatically
